attempts.label: DANDI:001195
attempts.entry_title: Dorsal raphe dopamine input to the BNST, CeA and BLP ex vivo (Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al. (2025) on dandiset 001195. The dandiset holds the ex vivo patch-clamp recordings of Figure 6 and Figure 7 supplement 1, which are tested here, and the in vivo CeA calcium imaging of Figure 7 without the pose or cup-interaction data its analysis needs. The behavioural, tracing and RNAscope data of Figures 1 to 5 and 8 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al. (2025) from dandiset 001195

outcomes.statement: At the resting membrane potential, photostimulation of DRN-DAT terminals evoked both excitatory and inhibitory post-synaptic potentials in downstream cells of the BNST, CeA and BLP (19, 36 and 48 cells recorded).
outcomes.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2; Figure 6D-F
outcomes.quote: Optical stimulation at the resting membrane potential evoked both excitatory and inhibitory post-synaptic potentials (EPSPs and IPSPs) in downstream cells
outcomes.notes: Under both readings every region has cells with an EPSP and cells with an IPSP. At 2 SD the BNST, CeA and BLP have 15, 37 and 54 cells with an EPSP and 11, 30 and 49 with an IPSP; at 3 SD 13, 35 and 53, and 6, 14 and 38. The same test also passes in a light-free window of the same traces, so it does not by itself show evoked responses; the contrast does. At 3 SD 92.7% of cells have an EPSP and 53.2% an IPSP after the light against 79.8% and 30.3% without light; at 5 SD 84.4% and 19.3% against 40.4% and 4.6%; 55 rest averages exceed 10 SD in the 200 ms after the light and 2 six seconds later. For IPSPs the contrast is weak at 3 SD (53.2% against 30.3%) and clear from 4 SD up (27.5% against 11.0%). At 2 SD most cells are mix (73 to 84%), at 5 SD most are excitation only (62 to 74%). The dataset holds 15, 38 and 56 ChR2 cells with usable 30 s rest sweeps where the paper reports 19, 36 and 48 (14, 35 and 48 from the mice labelled male), so the counts do not match and the claim is judged on the cells present, as the criterion says. 19 ChR2 cells have no such sweeps, and 2 (C51, C52) fire before the light in all of theirs.
deviations: The files do not record the light; the first pulse is taken 5.468 s into each 30 s light sweep, where the average responses start, with later maxima of the grand average about 33 ms apart (data check). Cells recorded only with other light protocols (20 s or 60 s sweeps, light at other times) are left out.

The paper gives no threshold for an EPSP or IPSP (measured by hand in Clampfit); the criterion's readings, 2 and 3 SD of the 5 s baseline of the average trace, are run, with 5 SD as a variant. Run in a light-free window of the same averages, 12 s after the light, the rule finds an EPSP in 94, 80 and 40% of cells and an IPSP in 67, 30 and 5% at 2, 3 and 5 SD.

Rest sweeps with an action potential in the 5 s before the light are left out of the rest averages (148 of 2437 ChR2 rest sweeps, in 28 cells), as the Methods hold cells at rest below threshold ('negative current was injected to hold the cell at a subthreshold potential', Ex vivo electrophysiology). 51 sweeps of P10 whose ch-1 is beyond +-10 nA and whose Vm is 0 mV are left out as failed; its other sweeps are kept.

The 17 ChR2 cells of subjects 23, C137 and C150, labelled female in the files, are kept although the Methods use male mice only: without them the dataset has 25 BLP cells with current steps, fewer than the 27 the paper clusters. Male mice only is run as a variant (notebook, last section).
Rest sweeps include those with a negative holding current (Methods, cells held subthreshold with negative current).

outcomes.statement: In cells made to fire by constant current, photostimulation increased firing in all BNST cells (5 of 5), while CeA (20 cells) and BLP (17 cells) cells showed either an increase or a decrease in firing.
outcomes.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2; Figure 6G-I
outcomes.quote: During spontaneous firing, BNST cells were universally excited whereas more diverse responses were observed with the BLP and CeA
outcomes.notes: In every reading (pooled or per-sweep IEI, 5 or 5.5 s baseline) both classes occur in the CeA (8 excited, 2 inhibited) and the BLP (4 to 6 excited, 7 to 9 inhibited), and the BNST cells that can be classed are excited (2 of 2). The third BNST cell (B7, one sweep) has no action potential (highest Vm -29 mV), so the paper's 5 of 5 cannot be checked. The dataset holds 3, 13 and 13 ChR2 cells with firing sweeps where the paper reports 5, 20 and 17. C29 and C47 (CeA) never cross 0 mV (highest Vm -59 and -49 mV), so a lower spike threshold would not give them an IEI; C39 and P9 lack an IEI on one side. As a variant, adding the rest sweeps that fire before the light with a measured current above +10 pA gives 5, 17 and 17 cells, with the classed BNST cells excited in three of the four readings.
deviations: The files do not record the light; the first pulse is taken 5.468 s into each 30 s light sweep, where the average responses start, with later maxima of the grand average about 33 ms apart (data check). Cells recorded only with other light protocols (20 s or 60 s sweeps, light at other times) are left out.

Firing sweeps are the 30 s light sweeps with a positive holding current in their description (Methods, "constant positive current was injected to elicit consistent spontaneous action potentials"). The measured current is below +5 pA in 11 of these sweeps and above +20 pA in 77 rest sweeps; a set that also takes the firing rest sweeps with a measured current above +10 pA is shown as a variant.
Action potentials are upward crossings of 0 mV, a standard choice.

The 17 ChR2 cells of subjects 23, C137 and C150, labelled female in the files, are kept although the Methods use male mice only: without them the dataset has 25 BLP cells with current steps, fewer than the 27 the paper clusters. Male mice only is run as a variant (notebook, last section).

outcomes.statement: The peak amplitude of the optically evoked EPSP differed between regions, larger in the CeA than in the BLP.
outcomes.source: Figure 6J, left
outcomes.quote: peak amplitude (Kruskal-Wallis statistic = 6.790, p=0.0335; Dunn’s posts-hoc tests: CeA vs BLP p=0.0378)

statistics.about: EPSP peak amplitude across BNST, CeA and BLP

outcomes.notes: The CeA median exceeds the BLP median in five of six rows, but of the criterion's four readings only reading (a) at 3 SD is significant, narrowly: Kruskal-Wallis H = 6.02, p = 0.049, Dunn CeA against BLP p = 0.043 (13, 35 and 53 cells; medians 1.9, 2.5 and 1.2 mV). Reading (a) at 2 SD gives p = 0.088, reading (b) p = 0.86 and 0.27. At 2 and 3 SD the rule finds an IPSP in 67% and 30% of light-free windows, so most excitation cells become mix and reading (b) keeps 19 and 48 cells. The one passing reading rests on one cell: without C15, whose rest average carries an evoked action potential, reading (a) at 3 SD gives p = 0.075 (Dunn p = 0.071). At 5 SD both readings are significant (p = 0.016 and 0.037), and reading (a) stays so without C15 (p = 0.026). With the mice labelled male only, reading (a) is significant at 2 and 3 SD (p = 0.022 and 0.014). The paper reports H = 6.790, p = 0.0335.

outcomes.statement: The trough amplitude of the optically evoked IPSP differed between regions, deeper in the CeA than in the BLP.
outcomes.source: Figure 6K, left
outcomes.quote: trough amplitude (one-way ANOVA, F2,31=8.150, p=0.0014, CeA vs BLP: **p=0.0014)

statistics.about: IPSP trough amplitude across BNST, CeA and BLP
statistics.n: 34 cells with an IPSP (from the degrees of freedom)

outcomes.notes: The readings disagree. With inhibition and mix cells at 2 SD (90 cells) the ANOVA gives F(2,87) = 0.28, p = 0.76. At 3 SD (58 cells) F(2,55) = 6.88, p = 0.0021, CeA against BLP Tukey p = 0.0031 and Holm-Sidak p = 0.0033, with the CeA mean trough deeper (-0.78 against -0.45 mV). The 3 SD reading is adopted (see deviations). At 5 SD (21 cells, one in the BNST, so two groups) the CeA trough is also deeper (p < 0.0001). Inhibition-only cells number 3 to 5, too few for the test. The paper's test has 34 cells; 58 is outside 34 +- 3.4, so the claim holds only in part. With the mice labelled male only the 3 SD reading also holds (49 cells, p = 0.0052). The question of the detection rule is for the paper's authors (findings).

Assumed the 3 SD reading, because it agrees with 5 SD, the threshold at which IPSPs separate from noise (19.3% of cells after the light against 4.6% in the light-free window), where the CeA trough is also deeper (BNST has 1 cell there, so only two regions are compared). The false-detection rate alone does not justify 3 SD over 2 SD; at 3 SD the rule finds an IPSP in 30.3% of light-free windows against 53.2% after the light, so more than half of the 3 SD IPSPs may be noise, as most of the 2 SD ones are (67.0% against 82.6%). The 2 SD result is shown and does not reproduce.

outcomes.statement: The optically evoked EPSP and the slow component of the IPSP persisted after TTX/4AP, so the responses were typically monosynaptic.
outcomes.source: Figure 6 supplement 1D-E; Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: the optically-evoked EPSP (upper panels) and slow component of the IPSP (lower panels) was maintained following application of TTX/4AP
outcomes.notes: No text field of the files names TTX or 4-AP: the 103 sweep descriptions, the session descriptions ('baseline' or 'episodic stimulation'), the 103 stimulus types of the sequential recordings table and the electrode descriptions ('no description'); general/ has no notes, protocol, slices or pharmacology field. So the sweeps recorded after TTX/4AP cannot be told from the others. The files may hold them among the light sweeps.

outcomes.statement: Hierarchical clustering of CeA cells on four baseline properties gave two clusters, late-firing cells (cluster 1) that were excited by DRN-DAT input and regular-firing cells (cluster 2) that were mostly inhibited.
outcomes.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3; Figure 6L, 6N-O
outcomes.quote: CeA cells in cluster 1 represented ‘late-firing’ neurons, whereas cluster 2 were typical of ‘regularfiring’ neurons ... with cluster 1 ‘late-firing’ neurons excited and cluster 2 ‘regular-firing’ neurons mostly inhibited
outcomes.notes: All 16 readings (ramp ratio absolute or from deflections, sag steady state 100 or 200 ms, detection 2 or 3 SD, IEI reading a or b) give two clusters of 27 ChR2 CeA cells (the paper has 26), a late-firing cluster (mean firing delay 415 ms, maximum frequency 32 Hz, sag 1.7 mV) and a regular-firing one (168 ms, 79 Hz, 5.7 mV). The late cluster is mostly excited (11 to 13 of 17 or 18 cells) but has 2 or 3 inhibited cells (C20, a mix with a negative area; C53, from its IEI; C41 at 2 SD) and 3 without response data, so not every cell is excited as the criterion requires; 6 of 9 or 10 regular-firing cells are inhibited, more than half. The readings agree; the first part of the criterion fails in all 16 readings and the second holds in all 16. With 5 SD labels the late cluster has one inhibited cell (C53) and only 3 of 9 or 10 regular-firing cells are inhibited, so both parts fail. The cells come from 14 subjects. The criterion has no partial clause and its first part fails in every reading, so the claim is not reproduced (agreed in verification round 3).

Response labels follow the Methods (Ex vivo electrophysiology, last paragraph), the IEI when the cell has firing sweeps, else the EPSP/IPSP class with a mix labelled by the sign of the 0-5.5 s voltage area; labels at 5 SD are a variant.
Features computed here from the raw sweeps; the paper's values (Source data 13) are not in paper/.

outcomes.statement: The two CeA clusters differed in all four input properties (ramp ratio, maximum instantaneous frequency, firing delay and voltage sag).
outcomes.source: Figure 6 supplement 1H
outcomes.quote: Unpaired t-tests for CeA – ramp ratio: t24=3.502, p=0.0018; max instantaneous firing frequency (max freqinst.): t24=4.698, p<0.0001, firing delay: t24=5.050, p<0.0001, voltage sag: t24=3.983, p=0.0006
outcomes.notes: Under all four clustering readings the two CeA clusters differ in ramp ratio (p = 0.0072 to 0.029), maximum frequency and sag (p below 0.0001) and firing delay (p = 0.0089 to 0.014), with |t(25)| from 2.32 to 6.32.
deviations: As fig6no-cea-clusters, with 27 cells (t with 25 degrees of freedom, the paper's 24).

outcomes.statement: BLP cells clustered into putative pyramidal neurons (cluster 1) and putative GABAergic interneurons (cluster 2); 93% of the putative pyramidal neurons were inhibited by DRN-DAT input and 62% of the putative interneurons were excited.
outcomes.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3; Figure 6M, 6P-Q
outcomes.quote: with 93% of putative pyramidal neurons showing an inhibitory response, and 62% of putative GABAergic interneurons showing an excitatory response
outcomes.notes: Every reading gives 28 BLP cells (the paper has 27) in a cluster of larger capacitance (77 against 37 pF) and lower maximum frequency (27 against 133 Hz), the putative pyramidal neurons (17 cells), and one of 11. Of the pyramidal cluster 64.7% (2 SD) or 58.8% (3 SD) are inhibited, against 93 +- 9.3%; of the other cluster 72.7% are excited, against 62 +- 6.2%. The direction holds, the percentages are outside tolerance. With 5 SD labels 41.2% of the pyramidal cluster are inhibited and 52.9% excited, so the direction fails at 5 SD. With the mice labelled male only, 22 cells, 56 to 63% and 83% at 2 and 3 SD; at 5 SD 44% and the direction fails.

Capacitance is taken by the Q-method from the 5 mV square pulses of the seal test, the only voltage-clamp test pulses in the files; the Methods use a 5 mV, 250 ms step and unpublished MATLAB code. No correction for series and membrane resistance is made, so the error of the estimate depends on each cell's own resistances.
Rheobase and firing delay also use the further step series from 220 pA up that six BLP cells have; the Methods describe steps from -120 to 260 pA.

outcomes.source: Figure 6 supplement 1I
outcomes.quote: unpaired t-tests for BLP – capacitance: t25=4.803, p<0.0001, max freqinst.: t25=15.48, p<0.0001, firing delay: t25=2.743, p=0.0111, voltage sag: t25=2.705, p=0.0121
outcomes.notes: Under both readings the BLP clusters differ in capacitance (t(26) = 3.69, p = 0.0011), maximum frequency (t = 7.58, p below 0.0001), firing delay (t = 3.98, p = 0.0005) and sag (p = 0.0021 and 0.0032). The split depends on single cells: leaving out each of the 28 cells in turn, all four tests stay significant in 24 cases; without P10, P19, P29 or P43 the clusters have 12 or 13 and 14 or 15 cells and the delay no longer differs (p = 0.053 to 0.063).

outcomes.statement: The total voltage area evoked by DRN-DAT stimulation differed between the two clusters in both the CeA and the BLP, and the EPSP peak amplitude differed between the BLP clusters but not between the CeA clusters.
outcomes.source: Figure 6 supplement 1J-K
outcomes.quote: EPSP peak amplitude, CeA: unpaired t-test, t17=1.40, p=0.180; BLP: unpaired t-test t22=2.34, p=0.029. ... Total voltage area, CeA: Mann-Whitney U = 22, p=0.0023; BLP: Mann-Whitney U = 29, p=0.0019
outcomes.notes: Under every reading the total voltage area differs between the CeA clusters (U = 97 or 101, p = 0.0001 or below; medians 0.66 against -0.73 mV s) and the BLP clusters (U = 38, p = 0.020; -0.25 against 0.57 mV s); the EPSP peak differs between the BLP clusters (t(24) = -2.43, p = 0.023 at 2 and 3 SD) and not between the CeA clusters (p = 0.097 to 0.21). With the mice labelled male only (18 CeA and 21 BLP cells with an area) the BLP tests are not significant (area U = 20, p = 0.11; EPSP peak p = 0.099 at 2 and 3 SD), while the CeA area test is (p = 0.0047 or below) and the CeA EPSP test is not (p = 0.076 to 0.25 at 2 and 3 SD). outcomes.statement: Clustering CeA and BLP cells together gave two clusters with a response pattern very similar to that of the separate clusterings.
outcomes.source: Figure 6 supplement 1L-N; Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In addition, clustering CeA and BLP cells together yielded a very similar result
outcomes.notes: In every reading (52 cells) the combined clustering puts the CeA late-firing cells with the BLP putative pyramidal cells and the CeA regular-firing cells with the BLP putative interneurons; the combined clusters agree with the separate ones in 51 of 52 cells. The excited CeA cluster (11 to 13 of 17 or 19 excited) is the one with the BLP pyramidal cells (10 or 11 of 17 inhibited), and the excited BLP cluster (6 of 8) is the one with the CeA regular-firing cells (5 or 6 of 8 or 10 inhibited), so the excited cluster is not the same in the two regions, as the criterion requires. Figure 6 supplement 1N appears to draw exactly this pattern (CeA excited and BLP inhibited in cluster 1, the reverse in cluster 2); checked as a variant, it holds in every reading at 2 and 3 SD and not at 5 SD. Whether the criterion misreads the figure is asked of a reader (questions/001195.yaml).

outcomes.statement: With the expression and illumination parameters used, social preference of ChrimsonR mice did not differ significantly across GH off, GH on and SI off.
outcomes.source: Figure 7E; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: We successfully optimized viral expression and illumination parameters to minimize changes in social preference with DRNDAT-CeA with ChrimsonR
outcomes.notes: The imaging files hold CNMF-E traces and footprints, the raw one-photon movie and a link to the behaviour video. They hold no pose estimates, cup interaction or position series, no epochs for the habituation and test periods and no record of which cup held the juvenile; the SLEAP model is not published. The social-object ratio needs the mouse's side and which side held the juvenile. The dataset holds 12 ChrimsonR mice, as Figure 7E says, and C370 has no GH on session. One frame of each behaviour video (notebook, data check) shows the arena from above with the mouse and both cups; the cups are covered, so which held the juvenile cannot be seen, and nothing in the files records it. Side times could in principle be tracked from the videos; that was not attempted.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the ex vivo patch-clamp recordings (Figure 6, Figure 7 supplement 1) and the in vivo CeA imaging of Figure 7. The tracing (Figure 1), behavioural optogenetics (Figures 2 to 4 and 8) and RNAscope (Figure 5) data, 17 of the paper's 38 findings in the claims file, are not in it.

The imaging files hold traces, footprints, the raw movie and a link to the behaviour video, but no pose estimates, cup interactions, position, habituation and test epochs, or record of which cup held the juvenile, which every in vivo finding needs. The SLEAP model is not published. None of the 8 in vivo findings can be tested.

The imaging files hold 869, 913 and 854 ROIs for the ChrimsonR mice in GH off, GH on and SI off, about twice the paper's 429, 441 and 484 cells, and 35, 138 and 89 for the TdTomato mice against 39, 61 and 76. Nothing marks which ROIs the paper kept (the Methods say non-neuronal objects were excluded by hand).

The imaging traces and movie are stated at 25 Hz. Their 19,211 frames last 768 s at 25 Hz, but the behaviour videos last 961 s (median); at the Methods' 20 frames/s the imaging lasts 961 s, within 4 s of the video in 40 of 41 sessions (the video of C386, SI off, lasts 800 s). The data support 20 Hz.

Every imaging file describes another experiment. The virus field names a GRIN lens in the mPFC and Chrimson in the BLA, the stimulus field 589 nm light at 20 Hz for 5 min, and the experiment description 5 min habituation, 5 min stimulation and 5 min without, where the Methods give a GRIN lens over the CeA, Chrimson in the DRN, 620 nm pulses (8 at 30 Hz every 1 s) and 5 min habituation then a 10 min test.

The patch-clamp files do not record when the light was on; the stimulus series of the light sweeps are zeros, and the protocol is named only in free-text series descriptions (103 distinct ones). The light time had to be read from the responses, and protocols with other sweep lengths put the light at other times.
No sweep or session is marked as recorded in TTX/4AP, so the recordings of Figure 6 supplement 1D-E cannot be identified.

In current clamp the injected current (ch-1) is stored with unit volts; its values (pA, following the holding current and the current steps) show it is current. The seal test, a voltage-clamp recording of current with a 5 mV square command, is stored as an IZeroClampSeries with units volts.

Two cells named with the BLP letter (P4x and P42 of subject C141) are labelled BNST in inferred_layer and targeted_layer; the 19 B-named files match the paper's 19 BNST cells. 51 light sweeps of one cell (P10 of subject in_vivo_9) hold a membrane potential of 0 mV and a ch-1 beyond +-10 nA, failed sweeps that are not marked. Subject ids are inconsistent ('4484' and '4484?', '235' and '235 cage', 'in_vivo_5' and 'in_vivo_5_2'), so whether these are the same animals is not stated; if they are, there are 17 subjects, not 20.

The dataset holds 15, 38 and 56 ChR2 cells with usable 30 s rest sweeps in the BNST, CeA and BLP, against the paper's 19, 36 and 48, and 3, 13 and 13 with firing sweeps, against 5, 20 and 17; 19 ChR2 cells were recorded only with other light protocols. 27 CeA and 28 BLP cells have all clustering features, against the paper's 26 and 27.

The files label three subjects female (23, C137 and C150; 17 ChR2 cells), where the paper says all experiments were in male mice. Without these cells the dataset has 25 BLP cells with current steps, fewer than the 27 the paper clusters, but the mice labelled male give 48 BLP cells with rest sweeps, the paper's count. So either the sex in the files or the paper's statement is wrong for them, or these cells are not among the paper's.

The holding current named in the sweep descriptions disagrees with the measured ch-1 current in 88 ChR2 light sweeps: 77 rest sweeps in 13 cells carry more than +20 pA (B16, described as -100 pA, carries +106 pA) and 11 firing sweeps in 6 cells less than +5 pA (C29, described as +35 pA, carries -57 pA). 148 of 2437 rest sweeps, in 28 cells, fire before the light.

For the paper's authors (fig6df, fig6j, fig6k). What decided that a cell had an EPSP or an IPSP at rest, and does Figure 6J include mix cells? A rule of 2 or 3 SD of the baseline of the average trace finds an IPSP in 67% or 30% of light-free windows, gives 90 or 58 cells for the IPSP test against the paper's 34, and makes the EPSP region effect depend on the reading.

For the paper's authors (fig6-s1jk and the clustering claims). Were the cells of subjects 23, C137 and C150, labelled female in the files, among the cells analysed? With them the voltage-area finding of Figure 6 supplement 1J-K holds; without them its BLP tests are not significant.

The capacitance of the BLP clustering came from custom MATLAB Q-method code on a 5 mV, 250 ms step, which is not published and whose step is not in the files; it was estimated here from the seal-test pulses.

The ChrimsonR sweeps described '+0.3mW blue light' and '+0.2mW blue light' begin with the description of the 635 nm red protocol, and nothing says whether they carried red pulses as well as blue light. This attempt reads them as blue light alone (Figure 7 supplement 1E-F), from their small responses.

entries.description: Tests the findings of Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al. (2025) on dandiset 001195. The dandiset holds the ex vivo patch-clamp recordings of Figure 6 and Figure 7 supplement 1, which are tested here, and the in vivo CeA calcium imaging of Figure 7 without the pose or cup-interaction data its analysis needs. The behavioural, tracing and RNAscope data of Figures 1 to 5 and 8 are not in the dandiset.
